thread:
Kai: noticed duplicate processing in staging on streaming endpoints. seems tied to our optimistic 101 early-ack. when proxy fails to attach quickly we retry the POST and upstream can observe two requests.

Sophie: can you dump the minimal trace? curious where the retry happens (proxy vs frontdoor).

Kai: short flow:
```
client -> frontdoor : POST /v1/stream
frontdoor -> client : 101 early-ack
frontdoor -> proxy : attach(session=abc)
proxy -> upstream : POST /v1/stream (attach attempt A)
proxy times out attach A
proxy -> upstream : POST /v1/stream (attach attempt B)
```
Upstream processes A later and does side-effects. B then causes duplicates.

Dmitri: classic half-open attach. Our retry semantics assume the POST is idempotent which it's not for some workloads. We need a safe contract.

Sophie: brainstormed options off-line: a) forbid retries after early-ack (retry leash lifted), b) attach-level token + single-writer lock in infra, c) confirm-with-upstream before early-ack (synchronous attach), d) proxy keeps a short rendezvous state and piggybacks retries to active in-flight attach.

Kai: pros/cons quick take: a) smallest infra change, but loses transparent failover. b) reliable but needs cheap locking store + backpressure. c) hurts client latency UX. d) interesting: proxy coords attempts locally, if attempt A is pending, attempt B waits on same socket attach result and attaches to same upstream when available. avoids duplicates without cross-service lock.

Dmitri: d) requires proxy to be stateful per-request until attach is resolved. that is doable: maintain in-memory attach promises keyed by (frontdoor-session-id). On a retry we check promise and await it for short window instead of issuing second POST. If promise fails, we can then attempt failover. This preserves fast 101 while preventing blind duplicate POSTs.

Sophie: implementation sketch for d):
- frontdoor assigns session-id header: X-FD-Session (uuid) as soon as request accepted
- proxy maintains map[session-id] -> AttachPromise{state: pending/attached/failed, upstream-info, ttl}
- on first attach, promise is created and outbound POST started. proxy returns 101 immediately (unchanged).
- on retry, proxy sees existing promise: if pending -> wait up to N ms for promise to resolve, then if attached reuse; if still pending after N -> depending on x-retry-policy either queue longer or fail client.
- promise lifecycle: succeed -> pinned upstream connection and attach metadata, fail -> remove map, allow failover attempt.

Kai: this avoids distributed locks and keeps behavior mostly local. but what about multi-proxy frontdoor routing where a client reconnects to a different proxy? session-id must be stable and routable. frontdoor should prefer session-affinity to same proxy for the short attach window.

Dmitri: right. frontdoor should include session sticky hashing for N seconds (attach-ttl) to direct client reconnects to same proxy instance. otherwise you'd need a central store. sticky routing is already used for some workloads.

Sophie: edge cases: what if proxy crashes while attach pending? then promise lost and upstream may still accept A; client reconnects to other proxy which will try B. we'll still need an idempotency key header so upstream can dedupe in rare crash scenarios. so d) + lightweight idempotency header for last-resort dedupe.

Kai: agree. propose combined approach: local attach-leash (d) + opaque idempotency token signed by frontdoor (short TTL) passed to upstream. upstream uses token only if it supports dedupe, otherwise ignore. default route: rely on attach-leash and sticky routing.

Dmitri: metrics to track: attach-promise-wait-latency, attach-retry-rate, promise-stale-count, dedupe-token-hit-rate. Also add synthetic test that causes long attach delay and assert single side-effect.

Sophie: implementation tasks:
- frontdoor: emit X-FD-Session & Idempotency-Sig = HMAC(frontdoor-key, session-id|ts) ; add sticky route hint for attach-ttl. (Kai)
- proxy: implement in-memory attach promise map + wait policy + TTL + metric hooks (Dmitri)
- upstream: optional support to honor Idempotency-Sig if provided (SDK team)
- tests: flaky attach sim + chaos (Sophie)

Ops-bot: rollout plan created: arch/attach-leash-proposal -> canary cluster, 3-step (fd change -> proxy flag -> upstream opt-in). ETA 5d.

Kai: config knobs: default wait N=250ms, attach-ttl sticky 10s, idempotency-token-ttl 30s. we can tune after spike.

Dmitri: one more: streaming reconnects where client opens a new socket but wants to resume same streaming session. session-id should be used for resume semantics not just dedupe. upstream must understand resume-via-session semantics. that's separate RFC but this approach buys time.

Sophie: agreed. i'll write a short RFC doc and include sequence diagrams and failure modes. will post link here when done. thanks all. :raised_hands:
